A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVD-based model-merging work, renamed from SFTM to STF. All pages, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v1 ends with references despite mentioning an appendix; v2 includes Appendices A–D, whose contents can be distinguished from relocated main-text material.

before.justification: v1 reports original merging results for vision models, T5, GPT-2 LoRA adapters, and Llama models, together with held-out-task evaluation and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical evaluations and reports additional comparator results, feature-preservation measurements, singular-vector removal experiments, and merging times.

M1.justification: The core procedure retains task-matrix subtraction, trimming, SVD, projection-preservation equations, and scaled reconstruction. v2 absorbs singular values into the merging coefficients, making its main formulation mathematically equivalent to v1's. Renaming SFTM to STF and expanding its explanation do not establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight vision tasks, seven T5 tasks, three data-to-text datasets, three Llama capability benchmarks, and six held-out NLP tasks. The vision evaluation moves to Appendix D in v2; it is not removed. New diagnostics use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds MetaGPT, Consensus TA, and Localize-and-Stitch to the T5 comparison; Knots and MetaGPT to GPT-2 LoRA merging; and MetaGPT to Llama merging. These are evaluated comparator additions in Tables 1–3, substantially expanding the comparison set.

E3.justification: Sensitivity evaluation changes from ViT-B/32 to T5-base, with scaling-factor bounds changing from 0.5–1.2 to 0.5–1.0 and sparsity bounds from 0.10–0.50 to 0.15–0.50. v2 also introduces unscaled feature-residual measurements and timing protocols using CPUs for TIES/PCB and GPUs for STF. Newly disclosed benchmark hyperparameters alone do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds layerwise feature-preservation diagnostics, removal of smallest versus largest singular vectors, and runtime analysis. It replaces the ViT task-count comparison with a T5 task-count/scaling interaction study. The task-matrix ablation retains T5 but replaces the two ViT cases with Llama. The held-out-task robustness results are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 3(b) introduces shaded bands around the three- and five-task curves, absent from v1 Figure 1(b). Neither the caption nor the text defines these bands or their calculation, so their statistical meaning is uncertain. Template averaging remains unchanged; v2 newly supplies template counts but no independent-run counts or confidence levels.

E6.justification: The T5 table revises the proposed method's average from 73.8 to 73.7 and Ties-Merging from 71.5 to 72.2, with corresponding per-task changes. New comparator, feature-preservation, singular-vector removal, and timing results substantially extend the evidence. Existing vision and held-out-task tables, and the proposed method's GPT-2 and Llama benchmark scores, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendices A and B add a mathematical feature-preservation measure and an explicit SVD/null-space derivation. Theorem 1 largely reformulates v1's existing linear-system derivation through coefficient reparameterization. Appendix C nevertheless retains a Sigma factor inconsistent with v2's main equation, introducing a formal inconsistency.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free, feature-preserving model merging and strong benchmark performance remain. v2 adds an explicit introductory claim that experiments verify a strong correlation between feature preservation and performance, supported by its new Figure 1. The renamed method does not represent a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting task count to optimal scaling, singular-value magnitude to feature importance, and runtime differences to hardware and matrixwise processing. Its new limitations section acknowledges that singular features lack explicit semantic identification, interference control relies on simple scaling, and SVD/linear-system costs remain limiting. These substantially extend the earlier discussion.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a method-code URL, PyTorch implementation information, A100/EPYC hardware, and benchmark-specific sparsity and scaling settings in Appendix D.2. It also specifies template counts, vision grid-search settings, and omission of trimming for Llama. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated setting changes. v1's convolution-kernel reshaping instructions are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and descriptions for MetaGPT, Knots, Consensus TA, and Localize-and-Stitch, plus PromptSource and Lindsey et al. It also adds an explicit comparison with RegMean in Remark 2 and removes some broad introductory citations. The principal related-work organization and positioning remain similar.

P1.justification: The introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around task-specific feature superposition. The method section is reorganized, vision results move to the appendix, and limitations and supporting appendices are introduced. The title, method name, and author information also change.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the single-column main text with a two-column layout, adds a conceptual method diagram and feature-preservation/removal plots, redraws the analysis figure, and adds a timing table. Existing comparison tables gain rows or move to appendices, including the unchanged vision and held-out-task tables.

improvement.justification: Additional relevant baselines, diagnostic experiments, explicit limitations, and reproducibility details make v2 easier to assess and reproduce. These benefits are tempered by unexplained plot bands and the inconsistent Sigma factor in Appendix C. The updated T5 comparison also leaves an inaccurate superiority statement: Table 1 shows 73.7 versus Localize-and-Stitch's 72.9, a 0.8-point lead rather than the stated 1.4. Overall, the additions provide a limited net quality improvement.
